headline: Profit dips on softer underwriting, buybacks continue

kpis.label: Net income avail. to common shareholders

summary_short: Arch Capital reported Q2 FY2026 net income available to common shareholders of $1,047M ($3.00 diluted EPS), down 14.7% y/y as net realized losses and a higher tax expense offset stable underwriting; the combined ratio widened to 83.5% (+2.3ppt y/y) while book value per share rose 2.8% q/q to $68.04.
summary_long: Q2 net income fell 14.7% y/y to $1,047M ($3.00 diluted EPS) as net realized losses of $17M swung from $229M in gains a year ago, offsetting higher equity-method income. Operating EPS fell to $2.56 (-0.8% y/y). Underwriting income fell 19.7% to $657M; the combined ratio widened to 83.5% (+2.3ppt y/y) on higher catastrophe losses (7.6pts vs 2.9pts) in Insurance and lower favorable reserve development, partly offset by stronger Reinsurance-segment development. Net premiums earned fell 8.1% y/y on non-renewals across Insurance and Reinsurance. Book value per share rose 2.8% q/q to $68.04; Arch repurchased $1.2B of shares. No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Diluted EPS fell as $17M of net realized losses (vs $229M of gains in Q2 2025) and a smaller FX/tax benefit outweighed underwriting and higher equity-method income.

drivers.metric: Net income avail. to common shareholders
drivers.explanation: Net income fell on the same net realized loss swing and higher income tax expense, per the company's own GAAP-to-operating reconciliation table.
Operating income fell 8.8% to $893M on lower underwriting income, but the per-share decline was largely cushioned by an 8.2% reduction in diluted share count from buybacks.

Combined ratio widened as the loss ratio rose 2.0pts on higher current-year catastrophe activity in Insurance (7.6pts vs 2.9pts) and smaller favorable reserve development, partly offset by stronger Reinsurance-segment results.
Premiums earned fell on lower net premiums written in Insurance (MCE Acquisition-related non-renewals) and Reinsurance (non-renewals, share reductions, increased retrocessions) over recent quarters.
Book value per share rose as retained earnings and other comprehensive income additions outpaced the quarter's $1.2B of share repurchases.
CEO cited solid underwriting performance across all three segments and Arch's diversified platform; no forward guidance was issued in the release.
